draft.title: What influences a major purchase
card: Many things shape what people decide to buy. Price is one: a person has a budget, so what they can afford limits their choices.
The finance available matters too. Whether a person can borrow, and on what terms, can decide what they are able to buy.
Marketing, such as advertising and special offers, can sway a choice. Convenience, such as a shop close by or easy delivery, can also tip it.
Age can change what people need and want. Ethical or environmental concerns, such as wanting low emissions, can lead people to choose one product over another.
draft.remember: People weigh several influences together, not just price, when they make a major purchase.

a.q: Priya wants a car but chooses an electric one because she wants to cut pollution. Which influence is this?
a.why: Priya's wish to reduce pollution is an environmental concern that shaped her choice. It is not finance or marketing, because neither is mentioned as the reason.
a.clue: Think about why she cares about pollution.

b.q: Tom could afford several sofas. He bought one from a shop that offered free delivery to his door the next day. Which influence is most clearly at work?
b.why: Free next-day delivery to his door makes buying easy, which is convenience. Price is tempting, but Tom could afford several sofas, so cost was not what decided it.
b.clue: He could afford others, so what made this one easier?

problems.detail: The right option, 'An ethical or environmental concern', is clearly the longest, so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The clue 'what made this one easier?' echoes the card's wording for convenience ('easy delivery'), which all but gives the answer away.
